text: The Patriots fell short on Thursday Night Football in Chicago, dropping a 30-24 decision to the Bears in a contest that showcased both encouraging moments and frustrating breakdowns—Drake Maye's film revealed both promise and areas needing refinement, while Caleb Williams and the Bears' offense proved too much to handle in Round 2 of what's shaping up to be a matchup worth monitoring. The absence of starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown clearly impacted New England's ability to protect Maye and establish consistent offensive rhythm, though Rhamondre Stevenson did his part by reaching a career-high in receiving yards and continuing his impressive two-way contributions as he approaches his sixth straight season of 100-plus carries. While the loss stings—particularly on a national stage—the film review and postgame analysis suggest the Patriots' defense and offensive line health will be key storylines heading forward, even as Stevenson's all-around play continues to be one of the few bright spots in an offense searching for consistency.
